items.situation: A product you bought online arrived damaged.
items.prompt:
You recently bought a coffee machine from an online shop, but when it arrived it was damaged.

Write a letter to the customer service manager. In your letter
• give details of your order
• describe the damage
• say what you would like the company to do

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
bullets: give details of your order
describe the damage
say what you would like the company to do
items.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to complain about a coffee machine that I ordered from your website on 3 May, which arrived in a damaged condition. My order number is CM48217, and the model is the Barista Plus in silver.

The parcel was delivered on 7 May. Although the outer box appeared to be in good condition, when I opened it I discovered that the glass water tank had a large crack along one side. In addition, the plastic cover on the top of the machine was broken, and several small pieces were loose inside the packaging. As a result, the machine cannot be used safely, as water would leak from the tank.

I would be grateful if you could arrange for the damaged machine to be collected from my home and replaced with a new one as soon as possible. If a replacement is not available, I would like a full refund, including the delivery charge of £6. I have kept the original packaging and can provide photographs of the damage if required.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Khalid Al-Mansour

plan.en: Formal: Dear Sir or Madam / Yours faithfully. One paragraph per bullet. Polite requests: I would be grateful if you could…

items.situation: Inviting a friend to visit your city.
items.prompt:
A friend from another country is planning to visit your country next month.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter
• invite your friend to stay with you
• suggest some places to visit together
• give some advice about what to bring

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear …,
bullets: invite your friend to stay with you
suggest some places to visit together
give some advice about what to bring
items.model:
Dear Sarah,

I was so excited to hear that you’re finally coming to Saudi Arabia next month! It’s been far too long since we last saw each other, and I’d love it if you stayed with my family and me while you’re here. We have a spare room, and my mum is already planning what to cook for you.

There’s so much I want to show you. We could spend a day in the old part of Jeddah, which is full of beautiful traditional houses with wooden balconies. If you’re interested, we could also drive up to the mountains near Taif, where it’s much cooler and there are amazing views. And of course, you can’t leave without walking along the Corniche in the evening and trying some fresh seafood.

As for what to bring, the weather will still be quite hot during the day, so pack light, loose clothes and a good pair of sunglasses. It can get chilly in the mountains at night, though, so bring a jacket too. Don’t forget comfortable shoes, as we’ll be doing lots of walking!

Let me know your flight details and I’ll pick you up from the airport.

Best wishes,
Noura

plan.en: Informal: first name, Best wishes. Use contractions, a warm tone, and some exclamations in moderation.

items.situation: Asking your manager for time off.
items.prompt:
You would like to take a week off work to attend a training course.

Write a letter to your manager. In your letter
• explain what the course is about
• say why it would be useful for your work
• suggest how your work can be covered while you are away

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mr Harris,
bullets: explain what the course is about
say why it would be useful for your work
suggest how your work can be covered while you are away
items.model:
Dear Mr Harris,

I am writing to ask whether I could take a week off work from 12 to 16 October in order to attend a training course in project management at the Riyadh Business Institute.

The course covers the main stages of planning and running a project, including setting budgets, managing risks and leading a team. It is taught by experienced professionals, and participants who pass the final assessment receive an internationally recognised certificate.

I believe the course would be very useful for my current role. As you know, our department will be launching several new projects next year, and I would like to take on more responsibility for coordinating them. The skills I would gain would help me to plan our work more efficiently and to keep projects on schedule.

Regarding my duties while I am away, I have spoken to my colleague Faisal, who has kindly agreed to deal with any urgent client enquiries. I will also make sure that all my reports are completed before I leave, and I will be available by email if anything important comes up.

Thank you for considering my request.

Yours sincerely,
Ahmed Al-Qahtani

plan.en: Semi-formal to a named person: Dear Mr Harris / Yours sincerely. Polite, no contractions, slightly personal (As you know).

items.situation: Complaining to the council about noise.
items.prompt:
There has been a lot of noise from a building site near your home.

Write a letter to your local council. In your letter
• describe the problem
• explain how it is affecting you
• suggest what the council should do

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
bullets: describe the problem
explain how it is affecting you
suggest what the council should do
items.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to draw your attention to a serious noise problem caused by the construction site on Palm Street, opposite my home at number 14.

Work on the site began about two months ago. Since then, heavy machinery has been operating from as early as 6 am, and on several occasions work has continued until after 10 pm. The drilling and the constant movement of lorries are extremely loud, and the noise can be heard clearly even with all the windows closed.

This situation is having a considerable effect on my family. My children are finding it very difficult to sleep, and their schoolwork has suffered as a result. I work from home three days a week, and I am often unable to make phone calls to clients because of the noise. My elderly mother, who lives with us, has also complained of headaches.

I understand that building work is necessary, but I would ask the council to limit working hours on the site, for example to between 8 am and 6 pm on weekdays only. I would also be grateful if an officer could visit the area to measure the noise levels.

Yours faithfully,
Mohammed Al-Shehri

plan.en: Formal complaint: specific details (times, places), the effect on you, then a reasonable practical suggestion.

items.situation: Apologising to a friend for missing their birthday dinner.
items.prompt:
Last weekend you did not go to a close friend’s birthday dinner, although you had said you would.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter
• apologise for missing the dinner
• explain why you could not go
• suggest how you could make it up to your friend

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear …,
bullets: apologise for missing the dinner
explain why you could not go
suggest how you could make it up to your friend
items.model:
Dear Sami,

I’m so sorry I missed your birthday dinner on Saturday. I know you’d booked the table weeks ago, and I feel terrible that my seat was empty.

I really did mean to come. Unfortunately, just as I was getting ready to leave, my mum called to say that my grandfather had been taken to hospital with chest pains. I drove straight there and spent the whole evening with the family while the doctors ran tests. Thankfully, it turned out not to be serious, and he’s back home now. In all the panic my phone battery died, which is why I couldn’t even text you. I hope you didn’t think I’d simply forgotten!

I’d love to make it up to you. How about I take you out for dinner next Friday at that new seafood place on the Corniche? My treat, of course — and I promise to bring your present, which is still sitting on my desk.

Let me know what works for you.

Best wishes,
Faisal

plan.ar: رسالة غير رسمية لصديق: Dear Sami ثم Best wishes. ابدأ بالاعتذار مباشرة، واشرح السبب بقصة قصيرة محددة، واختم باقتراح ملموس (مكان وموعد). استخدم الاختصارات (I’m, couldn’t) وأسلوبًا دافئًا.
plan.en: Informal: Dear Sami / Best wishes. Apologise straight away, explain with a short specific story, and end with a concrete offer (place and time). Contractions and a warm tone are fine.

items.situation: Thanking a neighbour who looked after your house.
items.prompt:
Your neighbour, Mrs Clarke, looked after your house while you were away on holiday.

Write a letter to your neighbour. In your letter
• thank her for her help
• tell her about your holiday
• invite her to your home for a meal

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Mrs Clarke,
bullets: thank her for her help
tell her about your holiday
invite her to your home for a meal
items.model:
Dear Mrs Clarke,

I just wanted to write and thank you for keeping an eye on our house while we were away. It was such a relief to know that someone we trust was watering the plants, collecting the post and checking that everything was secure. When we got back, the garden looked even better than when we had left, so you clearly put a great deal of care into it.

The trip itself was wonderful. We spent ten days in Malaysia, mostly in Penang, where the children loved exploring the old town and trying the street food. We also spent a day hiking in the national park, which was a highlight for all of us, despite a heavy downpour on the way back.

As a small token of our appreciation, we would love you to join us for dinner one evening next week. My wife is planning to cook some of the dishes we tried on holiday. Would Thursday at around seven suit you?

Thank you once again for your kindness.

Kind regards,
Omar Haddad

items.situation: Applying for a part-time job as a museum guide.
items.prompt:
You have seen an advertisement for a part-time job as a guide at a local museum.

Write a letter to the museum. In your letter
• say which job you are applying for and where you saw it
• describe your relevant experience and skills
• say when you are available to work

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
bullets: say which job you are applying for and where you saw it
describe your relevant experience and skills
say when you are available to work
items.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the position of part-time weekend guide at the City Heritage Museum, which I saw advertised on your website last week.

I am currently in the third year of a history degree, and I have a particular interest in the history of the Arabian Peninsula. Last summer, I worked as a volunteer at a heritage festival, where I led small groups of visitors around the exhibition and answered their questions. This experience taught me how to explain complex information clearly and engagingly, and how to adapt my approach for different audiences, including children. In addition, I speak fluent Arabic and English and have a basic knowledge of French, which I believe would be useful when dealing with international tourists.

I am available to work every Friday and Saturday, and during the university holidays I could take on additional shifts. I would be happy to attend an interview at any time convenient to you.

I enclose a copy of my CV and look forward to hearing from you.

Yours faithfully,
Reem Al-Qahtani

items.situation: Asking a college for information about an evening course.
items.prompt:
You would like to take an evening course at a local college.

Write a letter to the college. In your letter
• say which course you are interested in and why
• ask about the timetable and the cost
• ask whether there are any entry requirements

Begin your letter as follows:
Dear Sir or Madam,
bullets: say which course you are interested in and why
ask about the timetable and the cost
ask whether there are any entry requirements
items.model:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to enquire about the evening course in Digital Photography that is listed in your prospectus for the coming autumn term.

I have been taking photographs as a hobby for several years, but I have never had any formal training. I would now like to develop my skills further, particularly in portrait and landscape photography, as I hope to sell some of my work in the future.

I would be grateful if you could send me further details of the course. In particular, I would like to know on which evenings the classes take place, what time they start and finish, and how many weeks the course lasts. Could you also tell me the total fee and whether it can be paid in instalments?

Finally, I would appreciate it if you could let me know whether there are any entry requirements. For example, do students need their own camera, or is equipment provided?

Thank you for your assistance. I look forward to your reply.

Yours faithfully,
Ahmed Saleh
